script.title: Joint Products: NRV Method
script.caption_hook: One process, two products. How do you split the common cost?

lines.say: One process, two products. How do we split the common cost?
That's joint cost. One common method is to share it by net realisable value, or NRV.
Net realisable value? Sounds heavy. What is it?
Sales value minus further processing cost and selling cost, both after split-off.

board.title: NRV of a product
board.sub: S sales, F further cost, SD selling cost

lines.say: So we don't deduct the joint cost here?
Never. Joint cost is common. Only costs after split-off are deducted.
Joint cost is ₹65,000. A sells for ₹1,00,000, with ₹20,000 further processing cost and no selling cost.
So A's NRV is ₹80,000. What about B?
B sells for ₹70,000, with ₹20,000 further processing cost and no selling cost.
So total NRV is ₹1,30,000. Ratio eight to five?
Yes! Share equals NRV times joint cost, over total NRV. A gets ₹40,000, B gets ₹25,000.
Why not split by units produced?
Units ignore value. A low-value product would carry too much cost. NRV matches cost to ability to bear it.
Sell, Subtract, Split. Value decides the share!
